messages:
sarah: FYI — a customer (proj-42 / org-9) hit a confusing state: the per-project quota tile in the dashboard shows 0 remaining for the rolling window, but their API calls still succeed for a while and then suddenly 429s. Trying to reproduce. TL;DR: dashboard stale vs enforcement window? :thinking:

mike: can you paste the exact response headers & the dashboard screenshot margin?

sarah: screenshot uploaded to the ticket (link). curl response and headers here: 

```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED" \  -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":"hi"}' \  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-ratelimit-remaining: 0
x-ratelimit-reset: 1801210200
content-type: application/json

{"id":"gen_123","output":"hello"}
```

then ~20s later they hit a burst and got: 

```json
{"error":{"type":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"429: rate limit exceeded"}}
```

sarah: dashboard for proj-42 shows tile: "0 remaining (rolling 1h)" but org-level summary shows ~1.5k units available.

support-bot: Thanks — ticket #INC-3921 created and linked to this thread. :white_check_mark:

juhi: @sarah can you confirm the customer timezone / browser timezone? rolling windows are computed server-side but dashboard UI does timezone conversion for display which can confuse users. Also any chance they have multiple API keys used across different projects?

sarah: customer says all traffic uses the same project key (proj-42). They are in CET. I also pulled partial telemetry: 

```
telemetry_sample: {"project_id":"proj-42","org_id":"org-9","timestamp":1801209905,"window_start":1801203600,"tokens_used":1520}
```

mike: quick hypothesis: dashboard aggregation uses a pre-aggregated cache that updates every 30s, while enforcement uses a streaming counter with 1s granularity. If enforcement sees spikes while cache hasn't refreshed, UI could show stale "available" or the opposite depending on which surface you're looking at.

alex: also check for double-counting across fanout: if the org-level view sums project counters but the project-level tile is served from the quota ledger directly, there could be a mismatch when events are in flight between the ingestion pipeline and the aggregator.

eng-oncall: I'll run a live repro from our side against proj-42 keys in staging. Suggest we run: 

```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test-proj42" -d '{"input":"x"}' https://api.staging.redwood.ai/v1/generate >/dev/null &
done
wait
```

eng-oncall: planning to capture: request headers, x-ratelimit-* on each response, and the stream of ingestion events to the quota-aggregator. Will report within 30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

mike: nice. if we reproduce, next step is to trace the quota-window bucket boundaries (are we rounding to nearest minute? floor to hour?). Off-by-one bucket alignment could make the dashboard show last-window totals while enforcement uses current-window totals.

juhi: also flagging billing-bot — billing folks have seen related cases where invoice usage vs realtime meter diverged due to late-arriving events. @billing-bot any known TTLs?

billing-bot: Billing ingestion may accept late events up to 15m and still attribute them to the original window; the realtime dashboard is eventually consistent. If events land after the dashboard snapshot job, the tile could be stale until next snapshot.

sarah: customer wants an explanation & ETA. I'll say we are investigating and may need to escalate to runtime/ingest.

alex: if eng-oncall reproduces, please capture: 1) exact request timestamps (client UTC & server), 2) x-ratelimit headers, 3) aggregator commit offsets, 4) UI snapshot payloads (JSON). That lets us map enforcement vs display windows.

eng-oncall: captured logs: I see enforcement returned 429 at 1801210102 while aggregator commit for the same project had last update at 1801210060 (30s lag).

mike: that lines up with hypothesis. probable root cause: aggregator snapshot job has an occasional lag under burst; enforcement is authoritative (streaming counters). Need to decide whether to surface "approximate" state on UI or improve snapshot cadence.

juhi: propose short-term: update UI tooltip to say "Realtime enforcement may differ due to aggregation lag" and long-term: work with infra to reduce snapshot lag or push streaming metrics to dashboard.

sarah: customer updated: they understood and asked for an engineering note in the ticket. I'll post summary & link once we have RCA.

mike: assigning to eng-runtime and eng-infra to prioritize. I'll open an internal ticket with traces. :memo: 

sarah: thanks all :thumbsup:

support-bot: INC-3921 updated with logs and assigned owner: eng-runtime; next update expected EOD.
